messages:
maria: heads-up — seeing a cluster of traces with missing child spans when requests flow through grpc-mux and the otlp exporter starts throttling. started ~08:53 UTC, looks correlated with exporter_queue_overflow alert.

otlp-bot: alert: exporter_queue_overflow telemetry/otlp-exporter-0 at 08:53:12 UTC :warning:

aj: can you paste a small example trace or logs? wondering if traceparent is being dropped on a replay/flush path.

maria: here's a filtered log snippet from grpc-mux around the time (redacted ids):
```
[08:53:12] grpc-mux: Emit batch id=42 size=8 -> exporter-0 status=429
[08:53:12] grpc-mux: forwarded headers: traceparent=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-; tracestate=vendor1=abc
[08:53:12] exporter: queue overflow, dropping 3 spans (svc-b svc-c svc-d)
[08:53:12] grpc-mux: replaying batch id=42 -> exporter-1
[08:53:12] grpc-mux: forwarded headers: traceparent= (empty) ; tracestate=(empty)
[08:53:12] downstream svc-b: started span svc-b.handler id=xyz parent=NULL
```

# command i ran:
```
kubectl logs -n telemetry deployment/grpc-mux --since=20m | grep "Emit batch" -A3
```

sasha: we shipped a batching-window optimization last week to reduce small-batch churn. it groups by routing key, compresses identical headers, and then prunes empty header slots to save bandwidth.

kevin: iirc the prune logic treats an all-identical-header batch as "omit headers on replay" because we attach them once at emit time. that should be safe unless we replay to a different exporter instance that expects per-message headers.

lee: repro attempt: i tc-netem throttled exporter-0 to returns 429; observed that on replay to exporter-1 the traceparent field was missing consistently. stepping through grpc-mux replay path now.

aj: hypothesis: when exporter returns 429 we move items to a retry queue and re-serialize messages from the compacted in-memory batch. the compacted serializer intentionally elides headers and relies on an outer envelope, but the envelope isn't preserved on replay.

maria: confirmed — the envelope lives in the outgoing stream frame but the retry queue stores only the compacted payload. when we replay we reconstruct frames but the code path for header re-attach only runs for fresh emits, not for retries.

sasha: ugh. that matches the traces — child spans appear as root because traceparent got nulled. impact: partial traces across services, affecting dependency maps and alerts.

kevin: quick mitigation options: 1) revert prune to always include trace headers (cheap, high-impact), 2) ensure retry queue stores envelope metadata, 3) short-term rollback of batching-window flag.

lee: i'll open a local PR to reattach headers in the retry serializer and add an integration test that injects 429 mid-batch. can someone own the rollback toggle in case we need fast revert?

maria: i'll open an incident and assign oncall. tagging @aj for leadership on the release decision. i'm patching a small PR for option 1 to get it out quickly.

aj: thanks — please include a short regression test that runs with tc-netem to simulate exporter 429 and verifies child spans remain attached. also add a metric for "retry_replayed_without_headers" so SLO alerts can catch this earlier.

otlp-bot: incident created: INC-2026-431 — grpc-mux header-prune causing lost traceparent on retry (assigned to oncall).

maria: next steps: 1) patch + canary to dedicated cluster, 2) run synthetic traces through otlp pipeline, 3) monitor traces-per-request and dependency graph diffs. i'll post the PR link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
